# Pre-registered refinement criterion for n-butane central C-C-C-C dihedral scan

System: neutral singlet n-butane, gas phase. Coarse scan angles: -180, -120, -60, 0, 60, 120, 180 degrees, each with a constrained optimization holding the central C-C-C-C dihedral.

Acceptance rule: only converged constrained optimizations are treated as successful scan points. Non-converged points are retained and flagged, never presented as successful minima or extrema.

Refinement rule to apply after the coarse scan: plot relative electronic energy against the actual optimized dihedral. Refinement is indicated only if a suspected local extremum is bracketed by adjacent coarse points showing a sign change in the finite-difference slope and the energy difference across at least one adjacent interval exceeds 1.0 kcal/mol, or if one converged point lies more than 1.5 kcal/mol above both immediate neighbours. If indicated, add at most two previously uncomputed angles, placed at midpoints of the steepest bracketing intervals around the suspected extremum. If the curve is smooth or monotonic within numerical noise, or all adjacent energy changes are at most 1.0 kcal/mol, do not refine. The refinement decision is made only after coarse observations are returned to the main decision loop.

Random seed policy: any stochastic structure generation, search, or other algorithm will use seed 1701 and record it; if a library or model cannot fix a seed, that will be explicitly recorded as not fixable rather than fabricating determinism. The planned ORCA constrained optimizations are deterministic in this workflow.
